PlaNeRF is an unsupervised 3D plane regularization method for Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) designed to improve large-scale urban scene reconstruction.
It addresses geometric instability in low-texture environments by appending regularization terms to the photometric loss.

Unlike sibling methods that enforce a plane orthogonal to the center ray, PlaNeRF targets the least-squares plane approximation of a patch, allowing the surface normal to converge in an unsupervised manner.

GeCoNeRF is a regularization framework for few-shot Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) optimization that enforces geometric consistency across views using depth-guided warping and feature-level consistency modeling to overcome under-constrained optimization and overfitting.
It sets itself apart from pixel-level photometric consistency methods by operating at the feature level, which preserves view-dependent specular effects that pixel-level losses would suppress.
Unlike pre-training-based few-shot methods, it optimizes NeRF from scratch without requiring extensive multi-scene dataset priors.
